sources.title: Recovered question list containing the Promise.all prompt
Original Xiaomi front-end interview note description
Structured repository question record for Promise.all
ECMAScript Language Specification: Promise.all and PerformPromiseAll
Deterministic Node validation for the interview-level Promise.all helper

claims.text: The recovered source question is only 'promise.all'; it does not state that a polyfill, concurrency limiter, cancellation mechanism, or any particular implementation must be written.

Promise.all resolves each input through the constructor's promise resolve capability, records fulfillment values by the input index assigned during iteration, resolves with the resulting array only when the remaining-element count reaches zero, and routes rejection handlers to the aggregate promise's reject capability.

PerformPromiseAll initializes its remaining-element count with a sentinel and resolves an empty input after the iterator is exhausted; abrupt completion while obtaining or iterating the input is converted into rejection of the returned aggregate promise through the Promise.all algorithm.

The Promise.all / PerformPromiseAll algorithm attaches fulfillment handlers and the aggregate reject capability to converted input promises; the algorithm contains no operation that cancels or aborts other already-started input work when the aggregate promise becomes rejected.

The exact interviewPromiseAll implementation bytes are exercised by Node v22.16.0 tests covering empty input, ordinary values mixed with promises, reverse completion order with input-order result placement, thenable assimilation, first-observed rejection independent of array index, and an iterator that throws during iteration.

The candidate explicitly limits the handwritten helper to common interview-observable behavior and does not claim constructor-generic or step-for-step equivalence with the native ECMAScript Promise.all algorithm.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS cases=6 order=preserved thenable=assimilated first_rejection=observed iterable_throw=rejected
checks: ordinary values and promises are assimilated
completion order does not change input-order result placement
the first observed rejection settles the aggregate regardless of input index
an exception thrown while iterating rejects the aggregate

boundary_tests.case: second and third inputs complete before the first input
boundary_tests.expected: aggregate fulfillment values remain in original input order

boundary_tests.case: second input rejects before first input
boundary_tests.expected: aggregate rejection reason is the first observed rejection

boundary_tests.case: iterator throws after yielding one promise
boundary_tests.expected: aggregate promise rejects with the iterator error

findings: The candidate preserves the source boundary: the raw prompt says only Promise.all, so the answer distinguishes native semantics from the common but unstated hand-write variant instead of fabricating a requirement.

Input-order result placement, input conversion through the promise resolve capability, aggregate completion, rejection routing, empty-input behavior, and abrupt iterator handling are grounded in the ECMAScript Promise.all / PerformPromiseAll algorithm.

The cancellation statement is scoped correctly: the candidate says Promise.all itself does not add cancellation to already-started work, rather than claiming that cancellation is impossible for the underlying task.
The handwritten helper is explicitly described as interview-level rather than a complete native polyfill, which avoids overstating constructor-generic and internal-slot compatibility.
The deterministic Node fixture validates six observable behaviors against the exact implementation bytes referenced by code_validation.json.
No project metric or production experience is invented; the project-experience section stays at engineering tradeoff and boundary level.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate and is not treated as satisfied by this automated independent review.
